quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #5
										  					
  

33 Questions • Passing Score 27

questions.question: Fog makes it hard to see other vehicles, pedestrians, and traffic signals. What should you do when driving in fog?

options.text: Drive slowly and carefully.
Do not use your high beam headlights.
Use low beam headlights to see the road better.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Fog reduces your ability to see other vehicles, pedestrians, and traffic signals. When driving in fog, slow down and drive carefully. Do not use high beams. Use low beams instead because they light up the road better in fog.

questions.question: What is a good rule to remember about passing other vehicles?

options.text: Pass on the right whenever possible.
Drive with traffic flow and pass only when needed.
Move to the front of slow traffic so you can see better.
Always flash your lights and honk to alert other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive with traffic flow and pass only when needed.
questions.explanation: Each time you pass another vehicle, the risk of a crash increases. If you drive faster than other traffic, you will need to keep passing. Drive with traffic flow, stay within the speed limit, and pass only when necessary.

questions.question: What does a defensive driver do?

options.text: Drives slowly all the time.
Watches what other drivers are doing.
Drives at the same speed always.
Only drives in areas they know well.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watches what other drivers are doing.
questions.explanation: Even experienced drivers get distracted. A defensive driver watches what other drivers do and prepares for problems before they happen.

questions.question: Which statement is true about passing other vehicles?

options.text: Signal at least 100 feet before changing lanes to pass. Make sure no cars are coming toward you.
Check your mirrors and look over your left shoulder to see your blind spot when passing left.
See both headlights of the car you passed in your rearview mirror before moving back to your lane.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: When passing, signal at least 100 feet ahead. Always check your mirrors and look over your shoulder for your blind spot. Move back to your lane only when you can see both headlights of the passed car in your rearview mirror.

questions.question: When parking downhill on a two-way street, which way should you turn your wheels?

options.text: Turn your wheels to the right.
Turn your wheels to the left.
Keep your wheels straight ahead.
Leave your transmission in neutral.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your wheels to the right.
questions.explanation: When parking on a downhill slope, turn your wheels sharply toward the side of the road. If your car rolls downhill, it will roll away from traffic and be stopped by the curb.

questions.question: What should you do when an emergency vehicle with sirens and flashing lights approaches you?

options.text: Pull to the right and stop.
Pull to the right and slow down.
Pull to the right and turn on your four-way flashers.
Stop and let the emergency vehicle pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the right and stop.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle approaches with sirens, lights, or warning devices, immediately drive to the right side of the road and stop.

questions.question: What must you do when you see a funeral procession?

options.text: Do not drive between the vehicles in the procession unless a police officer tells you it is okay.
Do not enter an intersection if the procession is crossing through a red light.
Yield the right-of-way to vehicles that are part of the procession.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: State law requires drivers to yield the right-of-way to vehicles in a funeral procession. Do not drive between procession vehicles unless a police officer allows it. Do not enter an intersection while the procession is passing through.

questions.question: If two vehicles arrive at a four-way stop at the same time, what should happen?

options.text: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
The vehicle on the right must yield to the vehicle on the left.
Drivers must use hand signals to communicate.
One driver should go without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
questions.explanation: At a four-way stop, vehicles normally go in the order they arrive. When two vehicles arrive at the same time, the vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.

questions.question: What does a steady green light mean?

options.text: You must slow down and prepare to stop.
You must stop and check for oncoming traffic.
You may drive through the intersection if it is clear.
You may not turn right.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may drive through the intersection if it is clear.
questions.explanation: A steady green light means you can drive through the intersection if it is safe. You can also turn right or left on a steady green light unless a sign says you cannot. Always yield to other vehicles and pedestrians when turning.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: One-way traffic.
Divided highway ends.
Two-way traffic.
Keep left.

questions.correctAnswerText: Divided highway ends.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black markings on a yellow background. They warn drivers of upcoming hazards. This sign tells you that the divided highway is ending.

questions.question: How can you reduce the risk of hydroplaning?

options.text: Drive through shallow water.
Drive faster.
Drive slower.
Drive through deep water.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive slower.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when you drive too fast on wet roads. Driving slower reduces the risk.

questions.question: You are stopped in a line at a stop sign. The cars ahead pass through with no cross traffic. What should you do?

options.text: You may go through without stopping again.
You must stop at the stop sign before proceeding.
You may slowly roll through the stop sign.
You may follow the car ahead without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must stop at the stop sign before proceeding.
questions.explanation: You must always come to a complete stop at a stop sign and check for traffic before proceeding. Do not skip your stop just because other cars went through.

questions.question: What is the best way to handle a tailgater?

options.text: Speed up to get more distance between you.
Brake hard to make them back off.
Change lanes or slow down to let them pass.
Ignore them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes or slow down to let them pass.
questions.explanation: Watch your mirrors for tailgaters. If someone is following too close, slow down gradually to let them pass. Most rear-end crashes happen because drivers follow too closely.

questions.question: When can you carefully go through an intersection with a yellow light?

options.text: When an emergency vehicle is crossing your lane.
When pedestrians are crossing.
When you are turning right.
When you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow.
questions.explanation: If you are already inside the intersection when a yellow light appears, you may continue through carefully.

questions.question: Signs that tell drivers about dangerous conditions are called:

options.text: Regulatory signs.
Warning signs.
Information signs.
Guide signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning signs.
questions.explanation: Warning signs alert drivers to hazards ahead. Ignoring them can cause accidents and harm.

questions.question: Your wheels slip off the road edge. What should you do?

options.text: Jerk the steering wheel to get back on the road.
Speed up and steer back gradually.
Slam on the brakes and stop.
Gently brake and slowly steer back to the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gently brake and slowly steer back to the road.
questions.explanation: If your wheels leave the road, gently apply the brakes to slow down. Once you are going slowly enough, turn the steering wheel to return to the road. Do not jerk the wheel sharply.

questions.question: When a driver is turning and a pedestrian is crossing with no traffic light, who must yield?

options.text: Whoever started moving last.
The driver.
Whoever is slower.
The pedestrian.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver.
questions.explanation: Drivers must yield to pedestrians crossing at any intersection, with or without a traffic light or crosswalk.

questions.question: When parallel parking between two cars, what should you do first?

options.text: Turn your wheels to the left.
Turn your wheels to the right.
Pull up even with the car in front of the space.
Back up slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull up even with the car in front of the space.
questions.explanation: After finding a space and signaling, stop next to the car in front of your desired space. Then turn your wheels to park.

questions.question: Before making a right turn, your car should be:

options.text: Near the center of the street.
Close to the left side of the street.
Close to the right side of the street.
Past the center of the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Close to the right side of the street.
questions.explanation: To prepare for a right turn, stay as far to the right as possible. Do not cut across other lanes.

questions.question: When driving near large trucks, drivers must account for:

options.text: The longer stopping distance trucks need.
The shorter stopping distance trucks need.
The lower noise from trucks.
The higher speed of trucks.

questions.correctAnswerText: The longer stopping distance trucks need.
questions.explanation: Large trucks need more distance to stop than smaller vehicles. Stay where the truck driver can see you and where you can see the road ahead.

questions.question: An inattentive driver is someone who:

options.text: Looks at things off the road or daydreams while driving.
Looks at a passenger while talking to them during driving.
Only watches the car in front of them.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Do not get distracted by looking at passengers, searching your vehicle, reading, sightseeing, or daydreaming while driving. Keep scanning the road, checking mirrors, and looking at your dashboard regularly. These safe habits will help you stay focused as a driver.

questions.question: Hydroplaning is usually caused by:

options.text: Too many stops.
Sudden stops.
Sudden turns.
Driving too fast.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving too fast.
questions.explanation: Your tires cannot clear water from the road when you drive too fast. At high speeds, they lose their grip and the vehicle slides on a layer of water. This is called hydroplaning.

questions.question: This sign warns drivers about:

options.text: An upcoming intersection.
Road construction.
A curve in the road ahead.
Changes in traffic lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: A curve in the road ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you the road curves to the right ahead.

questions.question: What should you do if your vehicle's right wheels leave the pavement?

options.text: Stop quickly.
Pull completely off the road and wait before getting back on.
Speed up and steer back onto the road quickly.
Release the accelerator, slow down, then carefully steer back onto the road when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the accelerator, slow down, then carefully steer back onto the road when safe.
questions.explanation: Do not panic if your right wheels leave the pavement. Release the accelerator and steer parallel to the road. Slow down gradually. Keep both hands on the wheel and gently steer back onto the road. Check for traffic before returning to the pavement.

questions.question: When dealing with pedestrians, a driver must:

options.text: Make sure the pedestrian sees your vehicle.
Always give the pedestrian the right-of-way, even if they are wrong.
Give the right-of-way only when the pedestrian has the legal right to it.
Slow down and honk near a crosswalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always give the pedestrian the right-of-way, even if they are wrong.
questions.explanation: You must do everything possible to avoid hitting a pedestrian, regardless of who is at fault. As a driver, it is your responsibility to watch for pedestrians and give them the right-of-way at all times, even if they are crossing where they should not be.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Steep downgrade.
Crossroad ahead.
No right turn.
Narrow bridge.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steep downgrade.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. They tell drivers about upcoming road conditions and hazards. This sign warns you about a steep hill ahead. Slow down to protect your brakes and avoid accidents.

questions.question: A sign of a drunk driver is:

options.text: Weaving between lanes.
Driving slower than traffic around them.
Making quick or sudden stops.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Signs of drunk driving include speeding, weaving between lanes, driving slower than traffic, jerky movements, and sudden stops.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Road construction ahead.
The road curves left, then right.
The road curves right, then left.
Steep grade ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road curves right, then left.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you the road curves to the right first, then to the left. Slow down so you can safely navigate these curves.

questions.question: You are approaching a railroad crossing with flashing signals. You should:

options.text: Stop and look for a train.
Slow down and look for a train.
Look for a train, then speed up.
Do what the car ahead of you does.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and look for a train.
questions.explanation: When you see flashing signals at a railroad crossing, stop at least 15 feet from the nearest rail. Watch for other warning signs like lowered crossing gates or the sound of a train.

questions.question: Headlights must be used:

options.text: Only when traffic is heavy.
Throughout daylight saving time.
From 30 minutes before sunset to 30 minutes after sunrise.
From 30 minutes after sunset to 30 minutes before sunrise.

questions.correctAnswerText: From 30 minutes after sunset to 30 minutes before sunrise.
questions.explanation: Headlights are required from 30 minutes after sunset to 30 minutes before sunrise. They must also be used whenever you cannot see 500 feet ahead.

questions.question: What is a diamond-shaped sign?

options.text: A warning sign for road hazards.
An interstate route sign.
A school crossing sign.
A speed limit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: A warning sign for road hazards.
questions.explanation: Diamond-shaped signs are usually yellow and warn you about dangers ahead. In work areas, they may be orange. These signs tell you to be careful.

questions.question: What is the "No zone"?

options.text: The blind spots around a truck or bus where drivers cannot see.
A special speed zone.
A road where stereo volume is limited.
A TV show that replaced The Twilight Zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: The blind spots around a truck or bus where drivers cannot see.
questions.explanation: Large trucks and buses have blind spots on both sides, behind, and in front. Cars in these areas cannot be seen by the truck or bus driver. These areas are called the "No zone."

questions.question: You are driving at night and a car is coming toward you. What should your headlights be set to?

options.text: High beam.
Low beam.
Off, using only parking lights.
Either high or low beam.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam.
questions.explanation: Do not use high beam headlights when another vehicle is coming toward you or when you are following another car at night. Use low beam instead to keep everyone safe.
